notes: error_repair exercise items: sentences carrying typical English-L1 transfer errors. The learner produces the corrected sentence.

items.explanation: „volám sa“ already contains the verb — no extra „je“. English speakers add it because of „my name IS“.
„z“ changes the noun's ending: Amerika → z Ameriky. The noun's role in the sentence changed — watch the pattern.

items.broken: Môj starý otec narodil sa v Píle.
fixed: môj starý otec sa narodil v píle
items.explanation: „sa“ wants second position in the clause: „...otec SA narodil...“, not „...narodil sa...“ after the subject phrase.
Ordering puts the noun in the accusative and the numeral agrees: jednu kávu (feminine).
Slovak negation is a prefix on the verb: NErozumiem — not a separate word like English „not“.
